about: Step 2 of the non-exam-value spec (3 Oct 2026): this year's status for the 30 most-landed offered scholarship schemes, read on each awarding body's own page with curl (one request at a time, browser user-agent, Indian home connection). No AI, no aggregator date used as official. Input of scripts/apply-scholarship-cycle-reads-2026-10.ts, which writes only the `cycle` of the rows marked set-cycle or refresh-cycle into src/data/scholarships.ts (dry run by default). Times are IST, from the saved copy of each page.
review: Review fixes, 3 Oct 2026 22:00 IST. (1) Quotes are now visible text only: every saved page was re-parsed with HTML comments, scripts and default-hidden elements (display:none, pop-ups and modals with no live trigger) removed, and five first-read quotes turned out to be hidden text (HDFC CSR, Bidyarthi, LPF home, jsw.in, Sitaram Jindal). Hidden text is kept apart in `hidden` and is never evidence for a date or status. (2) lila-poonawalla-girls was re-read and its note rewritten from visible text. (3) ts-epaas: ePASS's post-matric services page was read. (4) Notes rewritten for gujarat-mysy (two exceptions on the same notice) and csss (the conflicting NSP statements, renewal action first). (5) `rowFixes`: field corrections read on the same official pages, written with the cycles in one logged, undoable edit (the script's --cycles-only or --skip-fix=<id>:<field> leaves them out). Second review, 3 Oct 2026 23:26-23:35 IST (the reviewer's re-reads are saved in step2-rereview/pages; no page was read again for these fixes, which rest on the saved 3 Oct copies): (6) csss's last date is now NSP's home-page 31-10-2026, sourced to https://scholarships.gov.in/, with the scheme card's 30-09-2026 kept in the note — if NSP is in fact closed, a renewal student loses nothing by trying, while 'closed' on an open portal costs the renewal. (7) Siemens and LPF eligibility (and Siemens's amount) are corrected from the same official pages as their cycles, because the step now prints an official 2026-27 status beside them: Siemens income ₹2 lakh, marks 50% (HSC, with SSC 60% and PCM 60% in the note), a note with its conditions; LPF's invented ₹6 lakh income gate is removed (its page names under ₹3.5 lakh 'or lower-middle class homes') and its note names its cities. (8) ts-overseas-bc's name keeps 'overseas scholarship' for search; ePASS's note names who its renewal link covers; Siemens's and ePASS's notes lead with 'open'. (9) The comment above each refreshed cycle says which older comment's date it supersedes. (10) 4 Oct 2026, review states: a cycle may now carry openNow (the official page says this year's applications are open; no last date) or rolling (applications taken at any time). openNow is set on siemens-india-scholarship and ts-epaas only — both pages were re-read at 06:45 IST on 4 Oct and still say so; not on lila-poonawalla-girls, whose pages do not say applications are open. rolling is set on ca-icai-scholarship (now set-cycle, with its usual-window prose corrected) after both ICAI pages were re-read at 06:39 IST on 4 Oct, byte-identical to the 3 Oct copies; not on sitaram-jindal, whose re-read pages do not say so. The Siemens and ePASS notes drop their leading "open" clause, which the date line now carries. (11) gj-mysy-fees, a second catalogue row for MYSY with the same dead apply link, is added at rank 31 as a companion of gujarat-mysy: the same reads, the identical cycle and the same applyUrl fix. (12) 4 Oct 2026, review fixes: ts-cm-overseas, a second catalogue row for Telangana's BC overseas scheme (both rows carried the name 'Telangana CM Overseas Scholarship (BC)'), is added at rank 32 as a companion of ts-overseas-bc: the same 3 Oct read of OverseasLinks.do, the identical cycle, the same name, categories and note fixes, the main row's amount text, and an apply link to ePASS in place of a host that does not resolve. ICAI's amount and eligibility note are corrected from the same flyer as its rolling state (parents' income up to ₹5 lakh for the needs-based scholarships, no income condition for the merit award, ₹1,500-₹5,000 a month by level); no matcher income gate is added. ePASS's note names the home page's own link text. Every cycle's checkedOn must now be a day on which its source page was read, and no earlier than readOn (checkReads), so a slipped release cannot move a checkedOn without a read of that page that day.

rowFixes.to: Students registered with ICAI for the CA Foundation, Intermediate or Final course (Final students must have started articleship). The needs-based scholarships ask that parents' income be no more than ₹5 lakh a year, certified by a practising chartered accountant (Foundation and Intermediate) or the articleship principal (Final). The ₹5,000-a-month merit award, for Intermediate rank holders 1 to 10 who have registered for Final and started articleship, lists no income condition. ICAI's flyer says an announcement on a revised scheme will be published on its Self-Service Portal shortly.
rowFixes.why: The row's note names a ₹3 lakh income cap. ICAI's flyer sets parents' income at no more than Rs 5,00,000 a year for every needs-based scholarship (Foundation, Intermediate, Final, and Final for Intermediate ranks 11-50) and lists no income condition for the merit award (Intermediate ranks 1-10). The page prints this note beside the new rolling line and in its eligibility FAQ answer (FAQPage JSON-LD). The row has no incomeMaxLakhs, so the matcher has no income gate for ICAI, and none is added: a ₹5 lakh gate would turn away the merit-award rank holders, for whom the flyer sets no income condition. The flyer's line on a revised scheme is kept, so a student knows the figures may change.
